title: A June DMI and ENSO product term gave no clear added autumn dipole forecast skill in 1981-2024
abstract: We tested whether a product of June Indian Ocean Dipole Mode Index (DMI) and June Nino 3.4 improves autumn DMI forecasts. The baseline used both indices and a linear time trend. Each fit used earlier years only, starting in 1950. Across 44 targets in 1981-2024, adding the product reduced mean squared error by 8.36%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -8.70% to 19.99%. Root mean squared error fell from 0.318 to 0.304 degrees C. The gain was 14.31% in 1981-2002 and -1.52% in 2003-2024. Five model checks also had intervals that included zero. This test gives no clear evidence of a reliable gain from this simple interaction. It does not reject ocean coupling or other nonlinear methods. Revised source products, a short record, model form and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, a retrieval recipe, numerical checks and a figure are included. External source records and yearly tables are not bundled.

display.caption: All six model comparisons have conditional intervals that include zero. Period scores show sensitivity to time span.

citations.reason: Prior June-index benchmark sets the baseline and source snapshots. Data overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
Prior tendency null motivates a test of a different response form.
